newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper seen down further, China zinc a puzzle.
newsitem.headline: LME copper seen down further, China zinc a puzzle.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) copper prices are seen heading lower later on Tuesday and may eventually test major support at US$2,100 a tonne, dealers said. "The next major area for copper is the $2,100 level," one dealer said. "It's certainly looking soft at the moment."
"If it breaches $2,100, it will probably go all the way down to $2,000," another trader said.
Speculative liquidation dragged LME copper down on Monday to a 7-1/2 month low and it was indicated at $2,135/40 in late trade. In Asia, copper was at $2,136/40 at 0230 GMT on Tuesday.
"It's really headed for $2,100, possibly late this week or sometime next (week)," a dealer said.
Broker Rudolf Wolff said in its daily review that "copper looks set for further downside tests, with next support at $2,140 then $2,130."
But the red metal is rapidly approaching the oversold level and "copper may experience a respite," Wolff added.
LME broker Brandeis said in its daily review copper could suffer more losses especially if "key support at the $2,080/$2,100 level is broken."

In the zinc market, Asian traders were divided over talk in Tokyo that Chinese smelters had now managed to cover large short positions in the metal and on the quantities of Chinese zinc said to be bound for the LME warehouse in Singapore.
One Singapore-based trader, quoting sources in Beijing and brokers who deal with the Chinese on the LME, said China has managed "to switch their positions."
"The Chinese have not only covered their shorts, they are in fact long in the market. They would very much want to see the market go up," he said.
But a Japanese dealer was more cautious.
"I think they're beginning to close their positions, but I'm not sure they've done so," he said.
Another trader believed the Chinese had "more or less covered their positions, but the price should be more active if they have managed to switch their positions."
The pace of zinc trading has been slow on the LME with the last trade seen on Monday $32 down on the day at $1,492 a tonne.
Dealers were also divided on how much zinc was on the way to the LME's Singapore warehouse.
"I understand about 25,000 to 35,000 tonnes is coming here in the next three weeks to a month to cover their shorts," a dealer said.
But other dealers feel the volume of metal being sent here will range between 3,000 to 6,000 tonnes.

"For very special reasons, the Chinese don't want to bring the material here because it would tip off the market," a dealer said. "I think there's still a big number in zinc here that is off-warrant."
The volume of zinc in the LME's Singapore warehouse reached 56,250 tonnes on Monday, unchanged from last Friday's report.
Asian physical base metal business was quiet, with spot aluminium premiums easing to around $80-$82 a tonne CIF Japan from last week's $80-$85.
